The name signifies the importance of continuous learning, self-improvement, and the pursuit of knowledge. In Islamic art and calligraphy, the word Itqan is often used to denote the highest level of mastery and excellence in a work of art.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Itqan holds great spiritual significance in Islam as it represents the attainment of complete faith and the realization of one's purpose in life. It is a reminder of the ultimate goal of every Muslim, which is to serve and please Allah. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is reported to have said that "There is a party of my community that will neither come to the mosque to sleep nor to drink [water], but they will enter Paradise." (Bukhari and Muslim). This hadith suggests that Itqan, or the completion of faith, can be achieved even in the simplest of daily acts, such as attending regular prayers or seeking knowledge. Itqan represents the fulfillment of one's spiritual journey and the attainment of eternal happiness in the Hereafter.
